title: podman-remote manifest add --artifact fails with blank error when no storage driver is set in storage.conf
body:
Description

  ### Issue Description

  `podman-remote manifest add --artifact` fails against a `podman system service` whose storage configuration does not set `driver =` (the case on openSUSE Tumbleweed, whose `storage.conf` has `driver = "overlay"` commented out). The client prints `Error: adding to manifest list <name>: ` with an empty message and exits 125.

  The same command works locally and works remotely when the service has the driver set explicitly (e.g. Fedora's `storage.conf`, or `--storage-driver overlay`).

  This breaks `test/system/012-manifest.bats` "podman manifest add --artifact-subject" for both root and rootless in the `remote` scenarios (openQA, Tumbleweed, podman 6.2.0):
  https://openqa.opensuse.org/tests/6343579

  ```
  not ok 48 [012] podman manifest add --artifact-subject
  # podman-remote ... manifest add --artifact --artifact-subject=containers-storage:quay.io/libpod/testimage:20241011 m-t48-...:1.0 /tmp/.../listed.txt
  # Error: adding to manifest list m-t48-...:1.0:
  # [ rc=125 (** EXPECTED 0 **) ]
  ```

  The failure is not specific to `--artifact-subject`; any remote `manifest add --artifact` fails.

  ### Steps to reproduce the issue

  On a host where no `driver =` is set in any `storage.conf` (no `/etc/containers/storage.conf`, no `~/.config/containers/storage.conf`, `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` unset), using a throwaway store:

  ```bash
  T=$(mktemp -d)
  podman --root $T/root --runroot $T/run system service --time=0 unix://$T/p.sock &
  sleep 3
  R="podman-remote --url=unix://$T/p.sock"

  $R pull quay.io/libpod/testimage:20241011
  echo hi > $T/listed.txt
  $R manifest create m:1.0
  $R manifest add --artifact m:1.0 $T/listed.txt; echo rc=$?
  ```

  ### Describe the results you received

  ```
  Error: adding to manifest list m:1.0:
  rc=125
  ```

  The server answers the `PUT /v6.2.0/libpod/manifests/m:1.0?...&artifactfiles=listed.txt&operation=update` with HTTP 400. The body, captured with a proxy on the socket:

  ```
  {"Id":"c8804e47d1144aa2148073c7e5a62c073ae873b57c70f2d99a31a268dadc6200","errors":["stat /tmp/repro.mErWfR/root/-images/c8804e47d1144aa2148073c7e5a62c073ae873b57c70f2d99a31a268dadc6200:
  no such file or directory"]}
  ```

  Note the directory name: `-images`, i.e. an empty driver name.
  
  ### Describe the results you expected

  The artifact is added and the manifest list ID is printed (rc=0). Failing that, the error text from the server should be shown instead of an empty message.

  ### Analysis

  1. `ManifestModify` in `pkg/api/handlers/libpod/manifests.go` (line 568 at v6.2.0) stores the uploaded artifact files with:

     ```go
     storageConfig := runtime.StorageConfig()
     fileDir, err := os.MkdirTemp(filepath.Join(runtime.GraphRoot(), storageConfig.GraphDriverName+"-images", manifestList.ID()), "")
     ```

     `StorageConfig().GraphDriverName` is the *configured* driver, which is empty when `storage.conf` doesn't set one, even though the store auto-selects `overlay` at runtime. The path  therefore becomes `<graphroot>/-images/<id>`, which doesn't exist. The in-code `FIXME` already notes that this is "a little too 'inside storage'". The real driver is available as
  `r.store.GraphDriverName()` (used in `libpod/info.go`), but `Runtime` has no public accessor for it.

  2. The client drops the message. The server does return the text in `errors`, but `podman-remote` prints only `adding to manifest list <name>: `, so the failure is invisible.

  Confirmation: with the driver set explicitly, the same sequence succeeds, and the subject also shows up in `manifest inspect`:

  ```
  $ podman --root $T/root --runroot $T/run --storage-driver overlay system service ...
  $ $R manifest add --artifact --artifact-subject=containers-storage:quay.io/libpod/testimage:20241011 m:1.0 $T/listed.txt
  f48a46c28921236fee1c829c7022e0ad765cfa70629a14e3ef1dfeb2d22b6aee
  rc=0
  ```

  SELinux is not involved. The kernel journal has no AVC at the time of the failures, and the SELinux-denial claim in the openQA comment has no evidence behind it.

  ### Suggested fix
  
  - Use the store's actual driver for the images directory (add e.g. `Runtime.GraphDriverName()` next to `GraphRoot()` and use it at `manifests.go:568`), or derive the path from the store  instead of rebuilding it.
  - Make `podman-remote` surface the server's `errors` text in the failure message.

  ### Podman in a container
  
  No
  
  ### Privileged Or Rootless
  
  Both (root and rootless fail identically in the remote runs)
  
  ### Upstream Latest Release
  
  Yes, v6.2.0. On `main` the code is unchanged since v6.2.0 (checked 2026-11-16).
  
  ### Additional environment details
  
  The test was added in #29669. It passes on Fedora because Fedora's `storage.conf` sets `driver = "overlay"`.
